Description

Histamine released from mast cells binds the H1 receptor on nociceptors. H1 activates Gq, whose α subunit stimulates phospholipase Cβ, and in sensory neurons this pathway sensitises TRPV1 through protein kinase C. RGS proteins end Gq signalling by accelerating GTP hydrolysis. The link to osteoarthritis rests mainly on epidemiology: users of H1 antihistamines show a lower prevalence of radiographic knee osteoarthritis.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, as it works for the block's result. The nucleotides and cofactors are olive. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: histamine excites nociceptors.
